steps_h2: Garment on Model Photo for Shopify
steps_lead: Upload the garment, choose a scene, then download a photo you can check against the real piece.

steps.d: Upload a clear garment photo showing collar, closures, sleeves, pockets, and hem. Flat lay or hanger both work if the shape is easy to see.
Pick an on-model scene. Ask for another pose, base layer, or back view only if needed. Generate when the scene matches the garment you sell.
Download the photo and add the real size chart beside it. Check fit and color against the physical piece before you post.

faq.q: What is AI virtual try-on for clothing?
faq.a: Upload a flat-lay or hanger photo and get that garment on a generated person. Use it beside the flat lay on the listing, or in the launch post.

faq.q: How do I get from a hanger photo to an on-model photo?
faq.a: Upload a clear garment photo, choose a fashion scene and download the result. Check shape, color, seams and closures against the physical piece before you publish.

faq.q: Which garments can I start with?
faq.a: Jackets, knitwear, dresses, skirts, shirts and trousers fit when the full garment is in frame. Keep the collar, sleeves, pockets and hem visible in the source.

faq.q: Can I make more than one scene from the same garment?
faq.a: Yes. Run the same photo again for a mirror, walk or lookbook scene. A back view needs a back-facing source or a clear description of the back, and it is a separate job.
Clothing shops, ecommerce teams and agencies that need an on-model photo without booking a model. The person in the frame is generated, not a hired model and not a customer.

faq.q: Do I need a photo studio to use it?
faq.a: No. The path on screen is upload, choose a scene, download. Start with a front or hanger photo and a simple pose.

faq.q: What does a try-on photo cost, and can I use it in ads?
faq.a: Each photo costs 24 credits, the cost is shown before you start, and a failed job returns those credits. The download has no watermark, and you can use it in your own ads, pages and posts.

faq.q: Can I use the square photo in an Instagram feed?
faq.a: Yes. The same square file can sit in a feed post and on the product page. Placement notes for that channel are on [AI Instagram ads](page:plat-instagram).

steps.prompt: Use the uploaded photo as the product and keep its shape, color and label area exactly. An adult model wears the garment and turns once in soft daylight to show the full silhouette, collar, sleeves, pockets and hem. Keep the pose relaxed and leave enough space for the complete outline. Natural fashion UGC look, eye-level handheld framing, one gentle push-in. Sound: fabric movement, no music. End facing camera with the garment centered for a listing review. Keep the background quiet and leave a clean edge around the garment for a listing crop.

reviews.h2: How Shops Use AI Fashion Model Photos
reviews.lead: A few ways clothing sellers put one garment photo to work.

items.t: New jacket on the product page
items.d: The shop uploads the hanger photo when the carton arrives and places the on-model frame beside the flat lay. Hem, sleeves and pockets are checked against the physical jacket before the listing goes up.

items.t: One standing scene for the drop
items.d: The boutique picks a single standing scene for the hero image of a new dress. Neckline, color and closures are compared with the garment on the rail before anyone posts it.

items.t: A back view from a second source
items.d: The label uses a back-facing source so the collar and rear seams can show. That second file is its own job, and the cost is shown before it starts.
The agency repeats upload, scene and download for each clothing client. People in the frames are generated. They are not hired models and not customers.
The square file goes on the product page, and the real size chart is added as text beside it. The photo does not invent measurements.
A puffer or coat is shown on a person instead of another hanger crop. Cuffs, pockets and hem stay inside the source frame so the result can be compared fairly.
